aboutIntro: Asterion Software is a small development studio specialising in backend systems, AI integrations and automation. On small and mid-sized projects, clients work directly with a senior developer.
aboutBody: This works particularly well when you need someone to understand the problem quickly and design a practical solution with minimal overhead.
diagramAlt: Diagram showing AI using documents, data, media and APIs to automate workflows, generate insights and trigger actions
faqIntro: Still have a question? Send us a message or call +420 604 257 866.
auditQuestion: How much does an AI audit cost?
auditAnswer: For a simple automation, a free initial consultation is enough and you then get a fixed-price offer straight away. For more complex projects, we first do an AI audit from CZK 14,900: we map your current process, tools and volumes, check the integration options and propose a fixed-price solution. If you then order the implementation, we deduct the audit price from it.
assistantQuestion: How much does an AI assistant cost?
assistantAnswer: A simple assistant that answers only from the materials you give it starts at CZK 9,000, whether it is internal for staff or on your website for visitors. An advanced internal assistant over company documentation and data has a pilot from CZK 35,000. Its price depends mainly on the number and type of data sources, integrations and access permissions. It answers using your documentation and cites its sources.
processAnswer: We start with a free initial consultation. A simple automation gets a fixed price straight away; for a more complex one, we first do a short paid AI audit. Every offer states what you get, what is not included and how we verify that the automation works. After handover, you can choose a flat fee for monitoring and operation.
contactQuestion: Who will I talk to during the project?
contactAnswer: You speak directly with the senior developer who designs and builds your solution, so questions can be resolved quickly and details stay clear.
excelQuestion: Can you turn our Excel spreadsheet into an app?
excelAnswer: Yes. We turn key spreadsheets and manual workflows into web apps with user accounts, permissions and change history. Projects typically start at CZK 45,000, depending on the data model and workflow.
trainingQuestion: Who is the corporate AI training for?
trainingAnswer: For employees who want to use AI in everyday work. We offer a three-hour AI Start course, a full-day Practical AI course based on your tasks, and an Automation Workshop for mapping processes.
ideaQuestion: Can I get in touch with just an idea?
ideaAnswer: Of course. Describe the situation in the form or give us a call. I’ll let you know whether we can help and suggest a next step.
contactTitle: Have a problem you’d like to discuss?
contactBody: Describe the situation in your own words. I’ll let you know whether we can help and suggest a next step.

deliverableGoal: a free initial consultation to clarify your goals,
deliverableScope: a short paid AI audit for more complex projects,
deliverableResult: a fixed price for a clearly defined scope and handover on your data,
deliverableFollowUp: an optional flat fee for monitoring and operation.
industriesTitle: Concrete use cases for your industry
industriesBody: We start with a free initial consultation. You then get a fixed price for a clearly defined scope, after a short paid AI audit for more complex projects. We measure the time before and after so the savings aren’t just an estimate.
exampleNote: An illustrative example of a typical company in the industry, not a specific client. The figures are estimates; we measure the real savings at your company.
calcTitle: How much does manual work cost you today?
calcBody: Enter how often the task comes up and how long it takes. The calculation assumes automation saves roughly two thirds of the time, which is a typical pilot target.
aiLiteracyDuty: duty under Art. 4 of the AI Act
trainingIndustryNote: We can also tailor Practical AI to your industry, for example for accounting firms, law firms or e‑shops.
dataAnswer: We design solutions so that data stays in the EU and the AI only works with what it needs for the task. We use business API access to AI models whose providers, under their terms, do not use the data for training. Hosting and access permissions are described in the solution proposal.
systemsQuestion: Will it work with our system?
systemsAnswer: Usually, yes. We connect via API, file export and import, or a shared mailbox, whether it’s an ERP, accounting software, an e‑shop or a shared drive. You keep your tools, and we add a new one only where it really saves work. During the initial consultation, we check which integration options your system offers.
mistakesQuestion: What if the AI makes a mistake?
mistakesAnswer: That’s why a person makes the call on important steps. The AI prepares the groundwork, a draft or a pre-filled record, and a person confirms it. The system flags uncertain cases and logs every action, so you can always trace what happened and why.
runningQuestion: How much does it cost to run after launch?
runningAnswer: The flat fee is optional and starts at CZK 1,000/month per automation, depending on AI usage and the number of integrations. It covers monitoring and operation: checking that the automation runs, error alerts, hosting, backups, AI fees and fixing errors on our side, with a response within 2 business days. Changes, such as a new bank statement format or new features, are quoted separately. Licences for third-party tools are paid directly to their vendors.
aiActQuestion: Does the AI Act apply to us?
aiActAnswer: Since February 2025, companies that use AI must ensure sufficient AI literacy among the people who work with it. AI literacy training helps you meet this duty. Stricter rules apply to high-risk uses, such as recruiting employees, and we take that into account from the solution design stage.

industries.name: Client documents under control
industries.description: The automation compares bank statements with client documents and prepares a list of what is missing, with a draft reminder. The accountant just approves it and keeps working in their accounting software.
scope: matching account transactions against documents in your accounting software
a list of missing documents for each client
a draft reminder email the accountant approves with one click
using the tools the firm already pays for
industries.example: A firm with 8 accountants and 120 clients spends about 2 days before each month-end close tracking down missing documents and writing reminders. Every week, the automation compares transactions on the clients’ accounts with documents in the accounting software. The accountant gets a list of missing documents for each client and a ready draft email to approve. The goal is to cut chasing from 2 days to half a day a month.

industries.name: Enquiry → job card
industries.description: Enquiries arrive by email with drawings in PDF and STEP. AI turns them into a job card, and the engineer just reviews and prices it.
scope: material, quantity, deadline and list of attachments
missing details and a draft follow-up question
lookup of similar past quotes
handover to the ERP
industries.example: A 15-person workshop receives about 60 enquiries a month, each with an email and several drawings. Today an engineer spends roughly 30 minutes preparing each one and has to follow up with the customer on a third of them. After rollout, they get a ready job card with a list of missing details and links to similar past jobs. The pilot target is to cut preparation to 10 minutes, saving around 20 hours a month and getting back to customers sooner.

industries.name: Fault reports under control
industries.description: Reports from email or a form are automatically assigned to the building, fault type and technician. The owners’ association board gets an overview without anyone writing it by hand.
scope: intake of reports from your existing email or form
duplicate alerts
tasks for technicians and updates for residents
monthly summary for the board and an overview of recurring faults
industries.example: A manager with 40 buildings receives about 150 reports a month by email and phone. The same fault is often reported by several residents, and boards keep asking for status updates. After rollout, reports are sorted automatically, duplicates are merged and the board gets a monthly summary. The goal is fewer status enquiries and a repair plan based on data about recurring faults.

industries.name: Returns and exceptions in fulfilment
industries.description: A return without an order number or a shipment status query no longer has to wait for someone to look it up manually.
scope: lookup of likely orders from the available details
a prepared case ready for review
handover of the confirmed status to the e‑shop
draft customer reply following the client’s rules
industries.example: A warehouse serving 25 e‑shops processes around 800 returns a month, and about 120 of them arrive without an order number. Today someone spends 10–15 minutes tracking down each one. The system suggests the most likely orders based on name, address and parcel contents, and a person just confirms. The goal is 2–3 minutes per return, saving around 18 hours a month.

industries.name: Email orders straight into the ERP
industries.description: Orders in PDF, Excel or the email body are entered into the ERP automatically. Sales staff only deal with unclear lines.
scope: extraction of items, quantities and customer
matching against the catalogue and price list
order creation in the ERP
for forwarders, transcription of transport orders and CMR paperwork
industries.example: A distributor receives 300 orders a month by email. Entering one takes 5–10 minutes, and product codes occasionally get mixed up. After rollout, the order is created in the ERP automatically and sales staff only check lines the system cannot match with confidence. The goal is to process over 80% of orders without manual entry and save around 30 hours a month.

industries.name: Candidate pre-screening
industries.description: Dozens of CVs per position, ranked against the requirements with a short rationale. The recruiter always makes the decision.
scope: sorting and summarising CVs
matching to open positions
draft personalised outreach and ATS integration
a record of why each candidate was recommended (AI Act)
industries.example: An agency with 6 recruiters receives 80–150 CVs per position, and the first screening takes a recruiter half a day. The system ranks candidates against the requirements and writes two sentences on why each one is or isn’t a fit. The recruiter starts from a shortlist and decides on every candidate personally. The goal is a first screening in an hour instead of half a day.

industries.name: AI for law firms
industries.description: Search across your own contracts, templates and filings, with links to sources. Users only see the case files they have access to.
scope: internal assistant for templates and the archive
first drafts of documents from templates
new client intake with ARES verification
access permissions by case file
industries.example: A firm with 10 lawyers has thousands of contracts and templates on a shared drive. Today a trainee lawyer can spend up to an hour looking for the right template or an earlier solution to a similar clause. The assistant answers with a link to the specific document and prepares a first draft from a template. The goal is finding things in minutes, with users only able to access the case files they have rights to.

industries.name: Product content at scale
industries.description: Descriptions, translations and visuals for hundreds of products at once, straight into your feed. Built on the same building blocks that power Studijo.
scope: bulk descriptions from specifications and photos
translations into SK, PL, DE and HU
feed optimisation for price comparison sites and Google
a consistent brand voice
industries.example: An e‑shop with 2,000 products wants to start selling in Slovakia and Poland. Writing descriptions and translations by hand would mean hundreds of hours of work or an expensive agency. Bulk generation produces descriptions and translations in a consistent tone, and the team reviews them in batches. The goal is to have the entire catalogue in three languages within a few weeks.

accounting.label: Accounting and tax firms
accounting.title: Client documents under control
accounting.intro: Before month-end, most of the time goes not into bookkeeping but into tracking down missing documents and chasing clients. Automation takes over that work while you keep using your accounting software.
problems: manually matching bank statements against documents, client by client
emails and phone calls to clients about what is still missing, then again
documents scattered across emails, photos and shared folders
keeping track of who has sent what only in your head or in Excel
the close drags on because the last documents arrive at the last minute

steps.title: We load bank transactions
steps.body: From the statement or a bank connection, every week or before the close.

steps.title: We match them against documents
steps.body: In your accounting software or in a tool you already use.

steps.title: We prepare a list and a reminder
steps.body: For each client, an exact list of missing documents and a draft email.

steps.title: The accountant approves
steps.body: With one click. Nothing goes to the client without the accountant’s approval.

principles: You keep your accounting software. We add a new tool only where it really saves work, and we set it up.
Clients install and sort nothing. They just email or photograph the document.
AI reads and suggests, the accountant decides. Uncertain values are flagged, never guessed.
Each client’s data is kept separate and traceable, processed in the EU under a data processing agreement.

accounting.firstOrder: The first project is deliberately small: one process, one accounting system and a small group of clients. We measure the time spent chasing documents before and after, so the savings aren’t just an estimate.
